The association between familial drinking and offspring drinking in young adulthood exhibits clear non-linear trends, with changes in the lower part of the familial drinking distribution strongly related to drinking in young adults. However, actual levels of drinking in families do not appear to be a significant predictor of the drinking patterns of their offspring in young adulthood.

This suggests that while there may be an influence from family factors on drinking habits, it is unlikely to play a major role in shaping the drinking patterns of young adults. In other words, the familial transmission of drinking patterns does not seem to persist into young adulthood in a straightforward or significant way.
